title: OpenAI adapter: streaming resilience, toolcall propagation, and metadata passthrough for Responses v2b
author: Liam Chen
description: Motivation: Customers using the new OpenAI Responses variants (v2b style payloads) reported gaps in compatibility when streaming tool/function calls and when propagating request-level metadata (seed/determinism flags and user-defined metadata) through the OpenAI adapter. This PR implements a compatibility shim that: 1) reliably reassembles structured streaming chunks (including toolcall boundaries and JSON-in-stream parts) into Redwood Response objects; 2) forwards seed/determinism and metadata passthrough to downstream runtime and to dedicated logging so we preserve determinism signals across retries/fallbacks; 3) hardens the streaming layer against mid-stream reconnects and duplicate chunk emission by adding idempotent fragment tracking and simple ACK semantics; 4) ensures tool/function calls are emitted as final structured events (not raw text) and include provenance metadata for RPC routing. The description below is one continuous string and includes checklist and testing notes. Checklist: - [x] Streaming reassembly with fragment-id dedupe - [x] Toolcall event boundary detector + structured emission path - [x] Seed/determinism flag propagation end-to-end - [x] Metadata passthrough into Redwood audit logs and response.metadata - [x] Integration tests for reconnect / duplicate-chunk scenarios - [x] Docs (compatibility guide) - [x] Backcompat smoke with existing openai adapter flows Implementation notes: - new module openai_adapter/response_v2b/stream_handler.py implements a streaming parser that tracks (stream_id, fragment_seq, fragment_id) tuples emitted by the Responses v2b stream. When we see duplicate fragment_id within the same stream we drop the second copy. Reassembly happens in-memory with optional bounded buffering; if buffering would exceed configured limits we fallback to file-backed spill and mark the response with partial:true and an explanatory note in response.metadata. - updated runtime/stream_reassembly.py adds a small interface so other adapters can reuse the idempotent fragment tracking and ack callbacks. - api/compat/openai_mappings.py maps Responses v2b tool_call events into Redwood toolcall objects and preserves the original tool call "tool_origin_id" and the request-level seed/determinism hint (seed_hint). - telemetry: added metrics openai.compat.stream.reassembled_count and openai.compat.stream.duplicate_fragments; traces annotate fragment counts and reconnections. - docs: docs/compat/responses_v2b.md describes expected wire shapes, streaming retry behavior, and recommended client-side idempotency keys. Testing and CI: - added tests/integration/test_responses_v2b_stream.py with simulated reconnects, duplicate fragments, and a long-running toolcall that is emitted as structured JSON. - CI matrix runs the new integration under both hosted and dedicated runtime mocks. Rollback plan: revert the head branch; adapter registration is behind feature-flag OPENAI_RESP_V2B_COMPAT so rollback is a config flip. Backcompat: default behavior unchanged for customers not enabling the feature flag. Release notes: "Adds an OpenAI Responses v2b compatibility adapter that improves streaming stability, preserves determinism seed flags, and forwards request metadata into Redwood responses and logs. Opt-in via OPENAI_RESP_V2B_COMPAT."

release_notes: Opt-in OpenAI Responses v2b compatibility adapter: streaming reassembly, deduplication of fragments, toolcall structured emission, and seed/metadata passthrough. Feature is behind feature flag.
notes_for_oncall: If customers report partial responses after enabling the adapter, check openai.compat.stream.reassembled_count vs stream.fragment_total and inspect for excessive disk spill events. Flip OPENAI_RESP_V2B_COMPAT=false to rollback immediately.
